title: The Woman Who Financed Jesus’ Ministry
paragraphs:
The Woman Who Financed Jesus’ Ministry
The Lesson I Learned From Joanna
Most people remember the famous names in the Gospels.

Peter.
John.
Mary Magdalene.
But hidden within the story of Jesus is a woman whose quiet faith helped sustain the very ministry that changed the world.
Her name was Joanna.
And most believers have barely heard of her.
Luke introduces her in a brief but powerful line:
“Joanna the wife of Chuza, the manager of Herod’s household… These women were helping to support them out of their own means.” (Luke 8:3)
That sentence may look small.
But the implications are massive.
Because it reveals something many people overlook:

The ministry of Jesus was not only carried by miracles and sermons.
It was also carried by faithful people who gave.

Travel required money.
Food had to be purchased.
Supplies had to be secured.
Thirteen men moving from town to town created real needs.
And Scripture tells us that Joanna helped provide for them.
She did not simply admire Jesus.
She invested in what He was doing.
Think about that.

While crowds were listening to Jesus preach…
While disciples were learning at His feet…
While miracles were drawing thousands…
There were also people quietly making sure the mission could continue.
Joanna was one of them.
But here is where the story becomes even more fascinating.
Luke tells us Joanna was the wife of Chuza, who managed the household of Herod Antipas.
That means Joanna lived close to power.
Her husband worked inside the political system of the man responsible for executing John the Baptist.
Yet despite that proximity to power, Joanna chose to align herself with Jesus.
Not the palace.
Not the empire.
Not the systems that looked strong.
She invested in a traveling Rabbi who owned almost nothing.
That decision required courage.
Supporting Jesus was not politically convenient.
It could have cost her reputation.
It could have created tension in her household.
Yet she still chose to support the mission of Christ.
And that reveals something profound.
Your investments reveal your convictions.
Many people say they believe in God.
But Joanna put her resources behind her belief.
Her faith was not just emotional.
It was practical.
It was sacrificial.
It was visible.
And the story does not end there.
Joanna’s name appears again at one of the most important moments in history.
The resurrection.
Luke 24:10 tells us that Joanna was among the women who went to the tomb and later told the apostles that Jesus had risen.
Think about that.
Joanna supported the ministry while Jesus was traveling.
Joanna remained faithful when Jesus was crucified.
And Joanna became one of the first witnesses to the empty tomb.
She was present in service… sorrow… and resurrection.
That is rare faithfulness.
Many people follow Jesus when the crowds are cheering.
But Joanna stayed when the story became painful.
When the Messiah they followed was executed.
When hope looked shattered.
She still showed up.
And God honored that faithfulness.
Here is the lesson many people miss:
Not everyone in the Kingdom is called to stand on the stage.
Some are called to sustain the mission behind the scenes.
Some preach.
Some go.
Some lead.
Some give.
And every one of those roles matters.
The Gospel story itself reminds us that the work of God often moves forward through hidden faithfulness.
Through people whose names are rarely preached about.
Through sacrifices no one sees.
Through generosity that never makes headlines.
Yet heaven sees it.
Joanna reminds us that the Kingdom of God is not built by visible voices alone.
It is also built by those who quietly carry the mission forward.
And that raises a powerful question for us today.
What are we investing our lives into?
Because money reveals priorities.
Time reveals priorities.
Energy reveals priorities.
Joanna had access to influence and resources.
And she chose to use them for the Kingdom.
She funded the mission that would eventually bring salvation to the world.
And most people never knew her name.
But God recorded it.
Right there in Scripture.
Forever.
Because heaven never forgets faithfulness.
Your obedience may not trend.
Your sacrifice may not be recognized.
Your generosity may happen quietly.
But what is done for Christ is never wasted.
Joanna teaches us that supporting the mission of Jesus is not a secondary role.
It is sacred.
It is strategic.
It is part of how the Gospel moves forward.
And sometimes the people who change history the most…
Are the ones who never stand in front of the crowd.
They simply choose to stand with Jesus.
And that kind of faithfulness still changes the world.

“Joanna… and many others were helping to support them out of their own means.”
— Luke 8:3
If this lesson spoke to you, take a moment and reflect:
Do you think the Church today overlooks the people who quietly support and fund the work of God behind the scenes?
